items.title: After 25 years on the throne, Selangor Sultan says people remain his priority
items.summary: His Royal Highness Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah said he would consider his reign meaningful if future generations believed he had fulfilled his responsibilities faithfully and placed the people first. Sultan Sharafuddin said buildings and infrastructure might change over time, but values, trust and unity would endure far longer. On the advice he would give his son, Raja Muda Selangor Tengku Amir Shah, who will one day succeed him as Sultan, Sultan Sharafuddin said the office was one of responsibility rather than privilege.

items.title: 54,506 Muslim divorce cases recorded nationwide in nine months
items.summary: According to Syariah Department data provided to Berita Harian, 44,603 cases have been resolved, 9,394 remain in proceedings, and 509 were categorised as archived. Syariah Judiciary Department senior director (judiciary) Abu Suffian Abu Yaziz said cases categorised as resolved include divorces through mutual consent, decisions delivered after trial, and court-ordered dissolutions. Abu Suffian said a lack of awareness regarding domestic responsibilities contributes to marriage breakdowns, despite couples having attended pre-marriage courses.

items.title: Fresh clashes rock France as protesters march on
items.summary: PARIS: Clashes erupted across France on Saturday as protesters took to the streets, a week after marches that degenerated into violence and prompted a firm security backlash from President Emmanuel Macron, who is scrambling to restore order. Police arrested nearly 1,000 people as officers faced "an extremely elevated level of violence" from black-clad "ultra-left" extremists, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said. Riot police squads fired tear gas at protesters in the capital as well as in Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Lille, Toulouse, Montpellier and Nantes.

items.title: Wawasan to consult PN partners before deciding on Melaka election
items.summary: Its president, Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainuddin, said the decision must be made collectively by all coalition members to ensure PN presents a united front. "God willing, what matters most is the agreement among our PN partners. The RoS had previously issued an order suspending all PN activities effective Sept 23.

items.title: ‘We cannot be pushed around’: MCA walks out of Melaka event, says Barisan ignored its say on seats
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 25 — MCA leaders walked out of a Barisan Nasional event in Melaka after objecting to what the party described as a candidate announcement and seat allocation process carried out without its agreement. “MCA cannot be pushed around. How can decisions be made on MCA’s behalf without our agreement when the MCA president is still here?”

items.title: Sarawak records highest API reading at 192, 12 stations unhealthy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Twelve air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8am today, with IPD Serian in Sarawak recording the highest reading at 192. According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Kuching recorded the second-highest reading at 187, followed by Samarahan at 183. Kota Tinggi in Johor recorded an API reading of 125.

items.title: 109 foreigners arrested in Ops Gegar raids across Ipoh
items.summary: IPOH: The Perak Immigration Department arrested 109 foreigners during two separate raids under Ops Gegar, including one at the Ipoh wholesale market early this morning. Immigration Department deputy director-general (operations) Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli said those detained were aged between 19 and 59. He said officers conducted the first raid around Ipoh at 9pm yesterday, while the raid at the Ipoh wholesale market began at 1.30am.

items.title: Delivery rider's death reclassified as murder after gig incident in Melaka
items.summary: MELAKA: Police have reclassified the death of a 21-year-old delivery rider, who was severely injured during a gig at a cafe here, as murder. Melaka Tengah police chief Assistant Commissioner Halim Abas said the incident, which occurred last Saturday, was initially investigated under Section 326 of the Penal Code before being reclassified under Section 302 of the Penal Code. He said the reclassification followed the victim's death on Oct 21, four days after suffering serious head injuries in the Oct 17 incident.

items.title: New York archdiocese agrees to pay US$800mil to sex abuse victims
items.summary: NEW YORK: The Archdiocese of New York said Saturday it had agreed to a settlement in which the church would pay more than US$800 million to hundreds of victims of sexual abuse by clergy. Before his departure, Dolan had announced the creation of a US$300 million fund to compensate sexual abuse victims. --AFP © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Expedite enactment of a comprehensive Clean Air Act
items.summary: LETTERS: The recurring haze affecting Malaysians should be a serious warning that we cannot continue to treat air pollution as a seasonal or temporary problem. Several areas have recorded unhealthy air quality, while the authorities have had to consider stronger measures when pollution reaches dangerous levels. Malaysia needs a stronger and more integrated legal framework to protect the fundamental right of our people to breathe clean and safe air.

items.title: 'Can't escape the burning smell': Johan Setia residents endure weeks of haze
items.summary: KLANG: A burning smell hangs over Kampung Johan Setia, where thick haze has lingered for weeks, leaving residents with itchy eyes, sore throats and coughs that refuse to go away. I see many of my customers falling sick, coughing. She said the acrid smell of burning was impossible to escape, even without stepping far from home, and was noticeably stronger in Johan Setia.

items.title: Open burning fuel persistent Johan Setia haze [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Open burning on farms and at illegal dumpsites is contributing to persistent haze in Kampung Johan Setia, Klang, where the Air Pollutant Index (API) has remained in the "unhealthy" range since August. Sungai Kandis assemblyman Wan Dzahanurin Ahmad said open burning, including on farms, remained a recurring problem in the area. He said open burning was also taking place in nearby areas, such as Kampung Sijangkang and Teluk Panglima Garang.

items.title: Trump casts early ballot as Republicans fight to retain Congress
items.summary: WEST PALM BEACH: US President Donald Trump on Saturday voted early in his home state of Florida for the Nov 3 midterm elections, in which his Republican Party is battling to maintain control of Congress. Trump said he voted party line, or exclusively for members of his Republican Party. "You ought to look at the real corruption – it's Democrat corruption," he said.

items.title: Thousands rally for Lula and Bolsonaro on eve of tight Brazil vote
items.summary: RIO DE JANEIRO: Copacabana beach turned red for President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva as hundreds of bikers revved their engines for right-winger Flavio Bolsonaro on Saturday, the eve of Brazil's nail-biter election. "The people must choose: either someone who kisses the national flag, or someone who kisses the American flag," Lula told the crowd. Bolsonaro, son of far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro, took a shock first-round lead with 47 percent of the vote over Lula's 45 percent.

items.title: Melaka polls: MCA president walks out of BN candidate announcement over seat row
items.summary: MELAKA: MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong walked out of the hall during the introduction of Barisan Nasional's candidates for the Melaka election last night, reports said. Sinar Harian reported that Wee left the hall at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) amid MCA's dissatisfaction with the seats allocated to the party for the election. He also said the party would not recognise the announcement of candidates made without MCA's consent.

items.title: Melaka polls: BN candidates must work harder to win, says Rauf
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Barisan Nasional (BN) candidates contesting the Nov 14 Melaka election must work harder to secure victory in their respective constituencies. Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said candidates entrusted to represent the coalition must prove their capabilities throughout the campaign. BN announced 21 candidates, comprising eight newcomers and 13 incumbents.

items.title: BN, PH to clash in 15 seats in Melaka polls
items.summary: Both BN and PH will contest 21 of the 28 seats up for grabs in the election. Caretaker Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, who will defend his Tanjung Bidara seat for the second time, will face PH candidate Mohd Yunazri Mustamiri. The following are the other 12 seats where BN and PH candidates will go head-to-head: Kuala Linggi BN: Datuk Rosli Abdullah (incumbent) PH: Muhammad Mukhlisul Mubin Julasapiyah Rembia BN: Ahmad Norazil Aziz PH: Mohd Khuzarie Mohd Kamal Kannan Gadek BN: S. Nadarajah PH: Jegasilan K Machap Jaya BN: Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem (incumbent) PH: Ginie Lim Siew Lin Durian Tunggal BN: Datuk Dr Mustafa Musa PH: Datuk Ashraf Mukhlis Minghat Asahan BN: Datuk Dr Fairul Nizam (incumbent) PH: P. Denesh Klebang BN: Datuk Lim Ban Hong (incumbent) PH: Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir Pengkalan Batu BN: Siti Aisyah Mahmood PH: Jason Tze-Xi Nathan Ayer Molek BN: Datuk Mohd Ridhwan Mohd Ali PH: Muhammad Hakimin Mokhtar Telok Mas BN: Datuk Abdul Razak Abdul Rahman (incumbent) PH: Captain (Rtd) Mohamad Jaafar Rim BN: Datuk Khaidira Abu Zahar (incumbent) PH: Esma Eazreen Husin Serkam BN: Datuk Azman Abdullah PH: Muhammad Faiq Azman © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Rauf: Melaka has no place for slander or hate politics
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Melaka has no place for slander or hate politics, as the state Barisan Nasional (BN) machinery gears up for the state election. BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh called on coalition members to embrace harmonious politics and maintain good relations with all parties to win voters' support. Melaka is not a land of hate politics.

items.title: Barbershops give Japan's yakuza their edge
items.summary: AT a barbershop in Tokyo, yakuza gangster Tekisasu glances in the mirror at his meticulous new cut and thanks the hairdresser for the weekly trim crucial to his mobster trade. "The yakuza are all about vanity," said Tekisasu, whose moniker means "enemy stabber", in an exclusive interview that took months to set up. Yakuza numbers dipped last year to a record low of 17,600 nationwide.

items.title: Trump comes knocking on Kim's door ahead of Apec summit
items.summary: AS world leaders prepare to gather in Shenzhen for next month's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit, speculation is mounting over a possible meeting between Donald Trump and Kim Jong-un — a prospect experts say remains remote. In 2019, North Korea's Kim made the 60-hour train journey home from Hanoi empty-handed after his summit with the US president collapsed. Trump said again last week that he "may" meet with Kim during his Asian tour next month and that it "would be exciting".

items.title: Anwar: Melaka must be developed by multiracial team, Malay interests safeguarded
items.summary: MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Melaka must be developed by a multiracial team that recognises the Malay community as the state's majority and a key pillar. he said at Stadium Hang Jebat tonight when announcing PH's candidates for the Melaka election. "Why exploit racial rhetoric?

items.title: NST Leader: Fix dangerous roads before the protests
items.summary: The use of coffins and mock graves in the protest marks a new low in public road safety and accountability. When residents feel compelled to stage a "theatre of death" to draw attention to dangerous road stretches, it marks a damning indictment of the authorities' responsiveness or the lack of it. In Kuching, residents living near Kuching International Airport have called for speed bumps along Jalan Sungai Tapang to curb speeding vehicles.

items.title: Zahid expects corruption allegations to feature in Melaka polls, tells BN to fight back
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi expects corruption allegations to feature prominently in the Melaka election campaign and has called on the coalition's machinery to counter them. Zahid, who is also Umno president, said attacks against caretaker Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, BN, Umno and its partners were likely to intensify as campaigning gathered pace. Zahid also called on BN members to maintain campaign discipline and refrain from spreading slander.

items.title: Foreign woman dies after being found submerged in Tanjung Bungah condo pool
items.summary: Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police received a report about the incident at 6.10pm. He said preliminary investigations found that the woman had been undergoing aquatic therapy with her husband at the pool at 5.20pm. Abdul Rozak said preliminary investigations found no criminal elements.

items.title: 9-month-old baby among four killed in Pagoh highway crash
items.summary: Pagoh Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Mohd Hafiz Mohd Shahid said the crash was believed to have occurred when the Ford Ranger carrying the victims rammed into a trailer parked by the side of the highway. "The four victims killed were two elderly women, a 5-year-old girl and a 9-month-old baby. "Other injured victims were travelling in the Toyota Vios, while the trailer driver escaped unhurt.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar unveils PH's 21 candidates for Melaka polls, Adly to defend Bukit Katil
items.summary: MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim tonight unveiled the coalition's 21 candidates for the Nov 14 Melaka election, with former chief minister Adly Zahari set to defend Bukit Katil. The others are DAP's Kerk Chee Yee (Ayer Keroh), Allex Seah (Kesidang), Low Chee Leong (Kota Laksamana) and Leng Chau Yen (Bandar Hilir). PH candidates for the Melaka state election: Kuala Linggi: Muhammad Mukhlisul Mubin Julasapiyah Tanjung Bidara: Mohamad Yunazri Mustamiri Rembia: Mohd Khuzaire Mohd Kamal Kannan Gadek: Jegasillan K. Machap Jaya: Ginie Lim Siew Lin Durian Tunggal: Datuk Asyraf Mukhlis Minghat Asahan: Danesh Palasubramaniam Paya Rumput: Datuk Azman Abidin Klebang: Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir Pengkalan Batu: Jason Tze-Xi Nathan Ayer Keroh: Kerk Chee Yee Bukit Katil: Adly Zahari Ayer Molek: Muhammad Hakimin Mokhtar Kesidang: Allex Seah Kota Laksamana: Low Chee Leong Duyong: Foo Long Suan Bandar Hilir: Leng Chau Yen Telok Mas: Capt (Rtd) Mohamad Jaafar Rim: Esma Eazreen Husin Serkam: Muhammad Faiq Azman Merlimau: Rahayu Hamzah The election will be held on Nov 14 to fill all 28 seats in the state assembly, which was dissolved on Sept 23.

items.title: Loke: Every ringgit recovered from corruption must benefit the people
items.summary: Speaking at Pakatan Harapan's candidate announcement for the Melaka state election at Stadium Hang Jebat tonight, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said billions of ringgit recovered under Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's administration should benefit the people directly. he said. he said.

items.title: [UPDATED] Melaka polls: Rauf, Akmal to defend seats as BN unveils 21 candidates
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Barisan Nasional (BN) has unveiled its 21 candidates for the Nov 14 Melaka election, including caretaker Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, who will defend Tanjung Bidara. Present were BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, deputy chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir and Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. BN candidates for the Melaka state election: Kuala Linggi – Rosli Abdullah Tanjung Bidara – Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh Ayer Limau – Datuk Hameed Mytheen Kunju Basheer Lendu – Datuk Abdul Hakim Abdul Wahid Taboh Naning – Datuk Zulkiflee Mohd Zin Rembia – Ahmad Norazril Abd Aziz Gadek – Nadarajah Selappa Machap Jaya – Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem Durian Tunggal – Datuk Dr Mustafa Musa Asahan – Datuk Dr Faizrul Nizam Sungai Udang – Datuk Rais Yasin Pantai Kundor – Datuk Tuminah Kadi Klebang – Datuk Lim Ban Hong Pengkalan Batu – Siti Aisyah Mahmood Ayer Molek – Datuk Mohd Ridhwan Mohd Ali Duyong – Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem Telok Mas – Datuk Wira Abdul Razak Abdul Rahman Rim – Datuk Khaidira Abu Zahar Serkam – Datuk Azman Abdullah Merlimau – Datuk Dr Akmal Saleh Sungai Rambai – Jezlee Pit © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: [UPDATED] 'Green has accepted blue': Zahid says BN must embrace new allies
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Barisan Nasional machinery and supporters must embrace the coalition's new political partners and help their candidates win in the Melaka election. BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said reciprocal support between BN and its strategic partners could pave the way for them to capture Putrajaya. Zahid said BN's machinery and voters must support its partners wherever they contested, just as their supporters would back BN candidates.

items.title: PH banks on stability, prosperity and good governance in Melaka polls
items.summary: MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan is placing political stability, economic prosperity, public welfare and good governance as the four main pillars of its offer to Melaka voters in the upcoming state election. Its secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the four pillars were essential to ensuring effective government administration and that development benefited all segments of society. Public finances must be safeguarded," he said.

items.title: Police record statements from 4 witnesses in boy's fatal fall
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Police have recorded statements from four witnesses following the death of a 7-year-old boy who fell from the 10th floor of a flat in Taman Perling yesterday. Acting Johor Baru Utara district police chief Superintendent Azrol Anuar Nor said initial investigations indicated that the boy had been playing with several other children along the 10th-floor corridor before the incident. He said the boy was believed to have used a bicycle to climb over the corridor wall before falling.

items.title: Azmin denies Bersatu supports appeal against PN deregistration stay
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali has denied claims that the party supports the government's appeal against a High Court decision staying Perikatan Nasional's deregistration. (hyperlink:https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/10/1559456/updated-ros-confirms-pns-deregistration ) Following the decision, Azmin said the deregistration vindicated Bersatu's earlier complaint against PN's leadership over alleged breaches of the coalition's constitution. ENDS KEYWORDS: Malaysia, Malaysia News, NST, nation, Bersatu, Azmin Ali, backs, RoS, Home Ministry, appeal, Perikatan Nasional, PN, deregistration.

items.title: Anwar chairs three major PKR meetings in Melaka before campaign launch
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 24 — Prime Minister and Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim attended three key party meetings held at around 3 pm today. The three important meetings, held at a hotel in Banda Hilir, comprised the State Leadership Council (MPN) meeting, the Central Political Bureau meeting and the PKR Central Leadership Council (MPP) meeting. Among the top party leaders who also attended the meetings were acting deputy president Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, secretary-general Datuk Fuziah Salleh, Wanita chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim and Melaka Leadership Council chairman Adam Adli Abdul Halim.

items.title: Two men found dead by riverbank after swimming in Sungai Tonggang
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 24 — Two men were found dead by a riverbank after swimming in a river, near Kampung Orang Asli Sungai Tonggang, Tanjung Rambutan, here today. Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant operations director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received an emergency call regarding the incident involving two victims, aged 42 and 50, at 2.55 pm. “The rescue team then brought both victims out from across the river before the Ministry of Health (MOH) medical officers confirmed their deaths at the scene,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Terengganu Sultan’s younger brother laid to rest
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 24 —The younger brother of the Sultan of Terengganu, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah, was laid to rest at the Royal Mausoleum of Masjid Al-Muktafi Billah Shah here today. The funeral rites for Tengku Baderul Zaman, who died at the age of 52, were completed at 6.10 pm. The Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, attended the funeral rites.

items.title: Selangor Sultan graces Royal Tea Reception in conjunction with Silver Jubilee celebration
items.summary: KLANG, Oct 24 —The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, today graced a Royal Tea Reception attended by 1,500 retirees, investors and civil servants in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee celebration of his reign at Istana Alam Shah here. Also in attendance were the Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, and the Raja Muda of Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah. At the event, Sultan Sharafuddin also launched the ‘Lakaran Indah Institusi Setiausaha Kerajaan Negeri Selangor’ book.

items.title: Public urged to stay calm during RTS Link security exercise on Oct 27
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 24 —The RTS Link Malaysia-Singapore Cross-Border Joint Exercise Field Training Exercise (FTX) 2026 will be held at the RTS Link Bukit Chagar Station and Wadi Hana Depot in Johor Bahru on Tuesday (Oct 27). The National Security Council (MKN), Prime Minister’s Department, said the exercise would run from 9 am to 5 pm and be conducted in collaboration with Malaysia Rapid Transit System Sdn Bhd (MRTS Corp) and RTS Operations Pte Ltd (RTSO). In a statement today, MKN said the exercise aimed to test and assess preparedness, response capabilities and coordination among Malaysian and Singaporean security agencies and emergency services.

items.title: Home Ministry leaves decision on charged AKPS chief to civil service process
items.summary: KULAI, Oct 24 — Matters concerning the position of Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain will be handled by the Home Ministry secretary-general and the Chief Secretary to the Government, said Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the matter was being handled by the two officials in accordance with existing public administration regulations. He was responding to questions on Mohd Shuhaily’s position as AKPS director-general while facing a court case.

items.title: DAP’s Yeo warns nationwide Waze ban could disrupt logistics and gig economy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — DAP national publicity secretary Yeo Bee Yin has cautioned the federal government against rushing into a blanket nationwide ban on the Waze navigation application, warning that a sudden prohibition would disrupt daily commutes, logistics, and gig-economy livelihoods for more than six million active Malaysian motorists. It directly impacts over six million active Malaysian road users who depend on real-time navigation daily for their livelihoods, commutes, and logistics,” she said in a statement. Waze has dismissed the data security allegations as "completely false", asserting that its global operations adhere to strict international privacy standards.

items.title: Two Malaysians injured in Typhoon Champi recovering in Taiwan hospitals
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Two Malaysian nationals who sustained minor injuries in the aftermath of Typhoon Champi in Taiwan are receiving treatment at separate hospitals and their conditions are reported to be stable. Malaysian Friendship and Trade Centre, Taipei (MFTC) President Bong Yik Jui said the two, both 57, were receiving treatment at Dali Jen Ai Hospital in Taichung and Miaoli Daqian Hospital in Miaoli, respectively. Bong said the MFTC would closely monitor developments related to Typhoon Champi, particularly its implications for the safety and welfare of Malaysians in Taiwan.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of heavy rain, strong winds in nine states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for nine states until 6 pm today. The warning covers Perlis, Perak (Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Larut Matang, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Batang Padang and Hilir Perak), as well as Langkawi and Kubang Pasu in Kedah. The warning also applies to Kota Tinggi and Johor Bahru in Johor; Cameron Highlands in Pahang; Dungun, Kemaman, Marang, Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus and Setiu in Terengganu; and Jeli, Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas and Tumpat in Kelantan.

items.title: Haze spreads to five Sarawak spots while Klang Valley air improves slightly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Air quality deteriorated further this afternoon, with 23 monitoring stations recording unhealthy readings on the Air Pollutant Index (API) at 4.00pm, up from 21 in the morning, according to the Department of Environment (DOE). Of the 68 stations nationwide, 23 registered readings in the unhealthy range of 101 to 200, while 39 recorded moderate air quality and six remained in the good tier. No station entered very unhealthy or hazardous territory.

items.title: Drunk driver crashes into DBKL road crew, killing supervisor on Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — A road maintenance supervisor was killed and a lorry driver injured early today when a suspected drunk driver crashed into them along Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the 26-year-old driver recorded a breath alcohol level of 64mg/100ml, NST reported. The lorry driver is receiving treatment at Kuala Lumpur Hospital.

items.title: End of the road: Sabah police nab Beverly Hills murder suspect wanted for over 17 years
items.summary: PENAMPANG, Oct 24 — A 42-year-old murder suspect on the run for more than 17 years has finally been arrested in Sabah over a 2009 homicide in Penampang. Penampang acting police chief Assistant Superintendent Arisanti Aziz said investigators detained the man at a house in Kolombong, Inanam on Thursday. Police had sought the suspect over the death of a man in Beverly Hills, Penampang on April 11, 2009.

items.title: Missing man found dead in locked car at Kajang supermarket car park
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — A man who went missing five days ago was found dead inside a locked car parked outside a supermarket in Jalan Impian Mahkota late last night, ending a desperate search by his family that had circulated on social media. Kajang district police chief ACP Naazron Abdul Yusof said authorities were alerted to the stationary vehicle at 11.29pm after passers-by spotted a motionless figure in the front cabin, NST reported. Naazron confirmed that the victim's family had lodged a missing person report last Tuesday after repeated attempts to reach his mobile phone went unanswered.

items.title: King and Queen offer prayers for late Terengganu prince Tengku Baderul Zaman
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The King, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, and the Queen, Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, have extended their condolences to the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, and the entire Terengganu royal family on the passing of Sultan Mizan’s younger brother, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah. “Condolences to Al-Wathiqu Billah Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Ibni Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah and the entire Terengganu Royal Family on the passing of Dato’ Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Ibni Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah. Tengku Baderul Zaman was reported to have passed away at 1.20 am today at a hospital in Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: PM extends condolences to Terengganu Sultan over brother’s death
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, on the passing of His Royal Highness’s younger brother, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah. In a Facebook post, Anwar also prayed that Allah SWT would shower His mercy upon Tengku Baderul Zaman’s soul, grant him forgiveness and place him among the righteous. Tengku Baderul Zaman died at 1.20 am today at Gleneagles Hospital here.

items.title: BN rejects Perikatan request for additional seats in Melaka election
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 24 — Barisan Nasional (BN) will stick to its agreement to allocate seven seats it is not contesting to Perikatan Nasional (PN) for the Melaka state election, despite attempts to secure additional seats. BN chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the allocation had been agreed upon under a mutual agreement, which BN would honour. Yesterday, PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man was reported as saying that PN hoped to hold negotiations to secure an additional one or two seats in addition to the seven announced earlier.

items.title: Malaysia stands ready to assist Yemen, backs renewed negotiations
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 24 — Malaysia stands ready to deliver humanitarian assistance to Yemen, while urging all parties in the protracted conflict in the country to return to the negotiation table and look for a diplomatic solution. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia empathises with the suffering of the Yemeni people who have to endure the effects of the protracted civil war, including famine and hardship in getting basic necessities. He said the matter was brought up by his counterpart, Yemen’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates, Dr Afrah Abdulaziz Al-Zouba, who shared on the latest developments in the country via a phone call on Thursday.

items.title: Government to establish Veterans’ Day for MAF veterans
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The government plans to establish Veterans’ Day to honour the service and sacrifice of Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) veterans. “It will also certainly foster closer ties and greater public appreciation for MAF veterans in our country,” he said at the opening ceremony of the 100th National General Assembly of the Malaysian Armed Forces Veterans Association (PVATM) here today. He said collections increased from RM1.3 million in 2023-2024 to RM2.19 million in 2024-2025 and RM3.35 million in 2025-2026.

items.title: PM Anwar calls for thorough investigation into detainee’s death in police custody
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered a thorough, transparent and uncompromising investigation into the death of Noorizwan Zulkefly in police custody. He said he understood the family’s grief and anxiety as they awaited answers regarding Noorizwan’s death. “I acknowledge the presence of the late Noorizwan’s family to submit an appeal letter to me today.

items.title: New-generation MyKad records 275,785 issuances in first month
items.summary: KULAI, Oct 24 — The National Registration Department (JPN) has issued 275,785 new-generation MyKad nationwide since its launch on Sept 17 until Oct 20, with Johor recording the highest number at 31,392 cards. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the figures reflected a positive response from the public to the new-generation MyKad, which comes with enhanced security features. He said the new-generation MyKad incorporates 53 security features, compared with 23 in the previous version, including a transparent window, QR code, ultraviolet features, hologram and microtext.

items.title: Cheras custodial death: Family takes plea to PM’s doorstep, seeks transparent probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The family of Noorizwan Zulkefly, who died earlier this month while under the custody of the Cheras district police, brought their fight for justice directly to the prime minister's doorstep this morning, demanding an independent and transparent inquiry into the circumstances surrounding his death. The memorandum, handed over by Noorizwan's younger brother Nooranis Zulkefly, expressed profound alarm over unexplained physical injuries documented during the post-mortem examination, urging Putrajaya to intervene directly to prevent an institutional cover-up. Pathologists at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM) in Cheras confirmed that while the post-mortem detected no structural trauma to internal organs, Noorizwan's body bore multiple external contusions and injuries.

items.title: Police probe local syndicate links after Indonesia seizes tanker carrying RM800m ketamine off Sumatra
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Federal narcotics investigators are working in close concert with Indonesian law enforcement to determine whether a Malaysian drug syndicate orchestrated the trafficking of 1.16 tonnes of ketamine hydrochloride aboard a coastal tanker intercepted off North Sumatra. The 57-metre Mongolian-flagged vessel, MT Global 168, was intercepted off Tanjung Balai Asahan on October 20 after Indonesian authorities linked its registered ownership to Johor-based firm Makmur Marine Petroleum. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan confirmed that Malaysian police were formally notified of the massive maritime interdiction by Indonesian counterparts yesterday, NST reported.

items.title: Kedah, Penang, Perak, Melaka, Johor and Sarawak put on thunderstorm alert
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has sounded a midday thunderstorm advisory for multiple states across Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak, warning of torrential rain, lightning, and gusty winds until 2.00pm today. In Kedah, stormy conditions are expected across eight districts, namely Kota Setar, Pendang, Yan, Kuala Muda, Bandar Baharu, Kulim, Baling, and Sik. Affected zones include Sebuyau in the Samarahan division, alongside Pantu, Lingga, and Sri Aman within the Sri Aman division, and Betong.

items.title: Wisma Putra: Two Malaysians suffer minor injuries after Typhoon Champi in Taiwan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Two Malaysian nationals are currently receiving medical treatment for minor injuries in the aftermath of Typhoon Champi on Taiwan, the Foreign Ministry said. The ministry which is also known as Wisma Putra said the matter was confirmed by the Malaysian Friendship and Trade Centre in Taipei, which is also providing the necessary consular assistance to both individuals. — BERNAMA TAGS: Typhoon Champi, Taiwan, Wisma Putra, consular assistance

items.title: Perikatan seeks talks with Perlis MB Abu Bakar snookered by two-term Bersatu suspension
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) leadership is aiming to broker a resolution to the political crisis in Perlis, seeking direct talks with Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah following his two-term suspension from Bersatu. Takiyuddin, who also serves as PAS secretary-general, noted that while Bersatu's disciplinary board had frozen Abu Bakar's party rights, the embattled state chief technically remains a Bersatu member. He noted that this restricts Abu Bakar from seeking refuge outside of Bersatu.

items.title: Sultan Mizan’s brother passes away; Terengganu declares three-day mourning
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 24 — The younger brother of the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman, son of the late Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah, passed away at 1.20 am today at Gleneagles Hospital, Kuala Lumpur. According to a statement by the Comptroller of the Terengganu Royal Household, Datuk Mohd Sophian Abu Bakar, the remains of Tengku Baderul Zaman will arrive at Sultan Mahmud Airport in Kuala Nerus at 1.15pm aboard a special aircraft. The Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail, will receive the remains of the late Tengku Baderul Zaman.

items.title: Sultan Sharafuddin calls for AI training, responsible social media use, geriatric care for Selangor’s future
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The Sultan of Selangor hopes future generations of Selangorians will be knowledgeable, compassionate, resilient, united and respectful of others. His Royal Highness Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah said young people should strive for excellence without losing their sense of responsibility towards society. Sultan Sharafuddin said the younger generation had rightly placed importance on environmental sustainability and heritage preservation.

items.title: Monarchy provides stability above political differences, says Selangor Sultan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Although society has evolved, the fundamental role of a constitutional monarch remains unchanged, the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, said. Sultan Sharafuddin said the Constitution provided clear guidance on his responsibilities. The monarchy, he said, represented continuity, stability, service and responsibility.
